### MMLU-Pro contradiction note

The HF model card lists **MMLU-Pro: 87.5%** for V4-Pro Max. The 91.2% figure that circulated in early write-ups is not present in any of the primary source files reviewed. Treat 87.5% as the canonical vendor-claimed number; 91.2% is unsubstantiated.

## Coding benchmarks vs frontier peers

Direct head-to-head numbers from the HuggingFace community blog ([source](https://huggingface.co/blog/deepseekv4)):

| Benchmark | V4-Pro | Claude Opus 4.6 Max | GPT-5.4 xHigh | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SWE Verified (resolved) | 80.6 **[V]** | 80.8 **[V via HF blog]** | not stated | Vendor claims parity with Opus 4.6 |
| Terminal Bench 2.0 | 67.9 **[V]** | not stated | 75.1 **[V via HF blog]** | V4-Pro 2nd to GPT-5.4 |
| MCPAtlas Public | 73.6 **[V]** | 73.8 **[V via HF blog]** | not stated | V4-Pro narrowly 2nd |
| Toolathlon | 51.8 **[V]** | not stated | not stated | V4-Pro best vs GLM-5.1 (40.7) |
| Internal R&D 30-task curated | 67% **[V]** | 70% (Opus 4.5) **[V]** | not stated | V4-Pro narrowly behind |

[MIT Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/04/24/1136422/why-deepseeks-v4-matters/) frames V4-Pro as *"matching the performance of Anthropic's Claude-Opus-4.6, OpenAI's GPT-5.4, and Google's Gemini-3.1"* but also calls it *"incremental progress, not revolutionary disruption like R1 achieved."*

[Simon Willison](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Apr/24/deepseek-v4/) is more reserved: *"V4-Pro trails state-of-the-art by approximately 3-6 months. Performs marginally below GPT-5.4 and Gemini-3.1-Pro on standard reasoning benchmarks."*

The two third-party framings are consistent with the vendor numbers if "matching" applies to coding-specific benchmarks while "trails by 3-6 months" covers reasoning/general intelligence.

## SWE-bench Verified credibility caveat

SWE-bench Verified is the highlight number on every V4 marketing surface, but the benchmark is contested as of early 2026:

1. **OpenAI retired Verified.** OpenAI's official retirement page returned HTTP 403 in this research session. Secondary reporting indicates OpenAI found *"structural contamination across all frontier models, not a model-specific issue"* — 59.4% of audited problems had flawed tests, and every frontier model tested could reproduce gold patches or problem-statement specifics.

2. **The Verified-vs-Pro gap is enormous.** [MorphLLM's SWE-Bench Pro leaderboard](https://www.morphllm.com/swe-bench-pro) (dated 2026-03-01) shows Claude Opus 4.5 at **80.9% on Verified vs 45.9% on Pro — a 35-point drop**. SWE-Bench Pro uses 1,865 multi-language tasks averaging 107-line modifications across 4.1 files, vs Verified's 500 Python-focused, mostly single-file edits. MorphLLM directly states: *"OpenAI confirmed that frontier models show training contamination on Verified's 500 Python-focused tasks."*

3. **Implication for V4.** V4-Pro's 80.6% Verified is vendor-claimed and not independently re-run by AA, MorphLLM, or BenchLM. Given the contamination concern, the headline should be read as "V4-Pro at the same level as Claude Opus on a benchmark that is now considered unreliable for cross-model ranking." V4-Flash's HF card reports SWE-bench Pro 52.6%; V4-Pro's card does **not** report a Pro number, which is itself a notable omission.

4. **MorphLLM data gap.** The MorphLLM leaderboard predates V4 (March 2026) and does not contain V4-Pro, Opus 4.7, or GPT-5.5 scores. A previously-circulated agent-search claim of "V4-Pro 55.4% / Opus 4.7 64.3% on SWE-bench Pro" is **not present** at the cited URL and should be treated as unverified.

## Long-context retrieval cliff

From the [HuggingFace community blog](https://huggingface.co/blog/deepseekv4), MRCR 8-needle accuracy curve for V4 family:

- **Through 256K tokens:** above **0.82** accuracy
- **At 1M tokens:** holds at **0.59**

A 23-point degradation between 256K and 1M. The advertised "1M context" is real but uneven — strong reliable retrieval up to 256K, sharply degraded at full window. The HF model cards report MRCR 1M MMR aggregate of 83.5 (Pro) and 78.7 (Flash), but the retrieval-cliff data is finer-grained and only available in the HF blog.

The KV-cache/FLOP efficiency story is what enables the 1M window: V4-Pro at 1M uses ~2% of a GQA-8 (bfloat16) baseline KV cache, 10% of V3.2's KV cache, and 27% of V3.2's per-token inference FLOPs. V4-Flash is leaner: 7% of V3.2's KV cache, 10% of V3.2's per-token FLOPs.

## Artificial Analysis cost-per-benchmark-suite

From [AA's overview](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/deepseek-is-back-among-the-leading-open-weights-models-with-v4-pro-and-v4-flash):

| Model | AA suite total cost **[3P]** | Output tokens generated **[3P]** |
|---|---|---|
| V4-Pro (Max) | $1,071 | 190M |
| V4-Flash (Max) | $113 | 240M |

AA quote: *"4x cheaper than Claude Opus, but pricier than most open-weights peers"* (V4-Pro). V4-Flash generates more output tokens than V4-Pro (240M vs 190M) yet costs ~9.5× less to run the same suite — driven entirely by per-token pricing ($0.17 vs $2.17 blended).

**AA Intelligence Index methodology** ([source](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/deepseek-v4-pro)) — aggregates 10 evaluations: GDPval-AA, Terminal-Bench Hard, τ²-Bench Telecom, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, IFBench, Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond, CritPt. Note: this is a different Terminal-Bench (Hard) than the vendor-reported Terminal-Bench 2.0.

## Confidence rating and gaps

**High confidence (multiple independent sources):**
- V4-Pro / V4-Flash architecture, parameters, context window, pricing — confirmed across HF cards, AA, Simon Willison, MIT Tech Review.
- AA Intelligence Index, hallucination rates, suite cost — single-source (AA) but methodology disclosed.
- KV cache / FLOP efficiency vs V3.2 — corroborated across HF blog, HF cards, Willison, MIT Tech Review.

**Medium confidence (vendor-only, no third-party reproduction in this evidence set):**
- All HF model card benchmark numbers (SWE Verified, LiveCodeBench, Codeforces, Terminal-Bench 2.0, GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro, SimpleQA-Verified, MRCR 1M, BrowseComp). AA evaluates on a different (overlapping) suite.
- The 80.6 / 80.8 SWE Verified parity with Opus 4.6 — both numbers come from DeepSeek's HF blog, not a neutral leaderboard.

**Low confidence / known gaps:**
- OpenAI retirement statement could not be retrieved directly (HTTP 403). Secondary reporting only.
- MorphLLM scores for V4-Pro and Opus 4.7 do not exist as of the March 2026 leaderboard.
- BenchLM rank #88 for V4-Pro Max ([source](https://benchlm.ai/models/deepseek-v4-flash)) is wildly inconsistent with AA's #3-of-77 ranking, indicating BenchLM's aggregation weights do not match AA's.
- No third-party verification of agentic benchmarks (MCPAtlas, Toolathlon) outside DeepSeek's own HF blog.

**Recommendation:** Quote V4-Pro / V4-Flash benchmark numbers with explicit "DeepSeek-reported" framing where they originate from the HF cards. Use AA numbers (Intelligence Index, hallucination rate, suite cost) as the primary third-party validation. Treat SWE-bench Verified scores with the contamination caveat unless paired with a Pro/Rebench cross-check.
